synopsis: Sixty Wells, day six. The Tamm Line comes in to sixty capped shafts and a slate board with nine numbers chalked on it. Sabra Onn, who was in this field in RR 166, tastes all sixty herself and says thirty-four has turned and fifty-one is sweet, and the board's keeper says it is one old woman's tongue. Denet Rasca settles it in a minute with a College-sealed water-glass — and the field goes on ration, not because the water changed but because the board did. Ysoly buys two hundred and twenty gallons at a block the hundredweight, cuts twenty-two blocks onto the debt face of the tally-stick, and owes the Assembly personally on her last crossing. That night Sabra asks Denet what else he has floated the glass against, and he tells her: the centre. The packet is cut open in Ysoly's cell before five people — forty-one leaves, no fair copy anywhere in the world — and Denet admits he wrote it, that he chose the Tamm Line because eleven is a small number of witnesses, and that Iseul Fane is the only Warden of the Third Rank between the rims. Nobody tells her. The line rolls south at dawn with the packet restitched in Pell Corrow's own waxed thread.
title: Reckoning at Sixty Wells
